FCCANALYSIS-SCRIPT(7) fccanalysis-script man page FCCANALYSIS-SCRIPT(7)

NAME

fccanalysis-script – analysis steering script specification

SYNOPSIS

*

DESCRIPTION

The analysis script is expected to be a valid Python script containing either part of or the full analysis. There are two basic modes how to run an analysis, one is to run in the managed mode like so:

fccanalysis run analysis_script.py

or

fccanalysis final analysis_script.py

where user needs to provide a set of required attributes and definitions in their analysis script. In this mode the RDataFrame is managed for the user and the analysis behavior can be controlled by providing additional attributes in the analysis script. The other mode is to run the analysis script as a regular python script:

python analysis_script.py

here user has full control over the RDataFrame, but has to create all necessary scaffolding.

Usually it is the case that the whole analysis will be split into several stages, which can be done in one of the two styles:

anascript_stage1.py -> anascript_stage2.py -> ... -> anascript_stage_final.py -> plots.py

or

analysis_histmaker.py -> plots.py

In the case of the first style there are at least three stages required (e.g. anascript_stage1.py, anascript_stage_final.py, plots.py) and there is no upper limit on the number of stages. In the case of the second style only two stages are required. The first style is named "staged style" and the second "histmaker style".

Staged style analysis
The analysis script needs to contain Analysis class of the following structure:
class Analysis():
def __init__(self, cmdline_args):
...


def analyzers(self, dframe):
dframe2 = (
dframe
# define the muon collection
.Define("muons",
"ReconstructedParticle::get(Muon0, ReconstructedParticles)")
...
)
return dframe2


def output(self):
return ["muons", "muon_mass"]

Histmaker style analysis
The analysis script needs to contain build_graph function of the following structure:
def build_graph(df, dataset):
results = []
df = df.Define("weight", "1.0")
weightsum = df.Sum("weight")
df = df.Define("muons", "FCCAnalyses::ReconstructedParticle::sel_p(20)(muons_all)")
...
results.append(df.Histo1D(("muons_p_cut0", "", *bins_p_mu), "muons_p"))
return results, weightsum
Final and Plots stages
These stages do not require Analysis class neither build_graph function, they have their own set of attributes, please see the examples in the examples of FCCAnalyses repository or fccanalysis-final-script(7) and fccanalysis-plots-script(7) manual pages.

ATTRIBUTES

In case of running the FCCAnalysis in the staged style user can/should add the following attributes to the Analysis class in order to control the behavior of the analysis.

samples
Dictionary of process samples to be run over. Analysis.process_list is deprecated; use Analysis.samples instead. Each sample can have several parameters:
Set at most one of input-dir, input-files, input-file-list, and input-lfn-list for a sample. A per-sample input source overrides the global input_dir. For the normal runner, the global directory overrides campaign discovery, and command-line input options override analysis-script input configuration. The local runner rejects LFN configuration unless direct command-line input overrides it or test mode uses a separate test file. Grid XRootD mode uses per-sample or global sources; campaign discovery is not available in that mode. Grid LFN mode can use --input-lfn-list, Analysis.input_lfn_list, or per-sample input-lfn-list. One submission cannot mix LFN and XRootD input. Duplicate input paths or LFNs within one sample are rejected. Explicit file paths and list entries retain their supplied order; files found within a directory are sorted by path.
fraction
Selects whole input files to approximate the requested fraction of total events. The fraction must be greater than zero and at most one. For DIRAC LFN input, fractions other than 1 are not supported.
Default value: 1 (process full sample)
input-dir
Specifies a directory for the process instead of the global one. For grid XRootD submission, provide a supported EOS path or an XRootD directory URL. The deprecated spelling input_dir remains accepted as a compatibility alias.
Default value: None
input-files
Non-empty list of non-empty input file paths or URLs for this process. Directory paths in this list are expanded to their immediate .root files.
Default value: None
input-file-list
Path to a text file containing one explicit input file path or URL per line. Directory entries are not expanded. Blank lines and lines beginning with "#" are ignored. This list contains physical file paths or URLs. For DIRAC LFNs, use the sample's input-lfn-list setting.
Default value: None
input-lfn-list
Path to a .txt file containing one DIRAC LFN per line. Blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored. This is available only for grid submission. All samples in one grid submission must use either LFN input or physical XRootD input; mixing the two is rejected.
Default value: None
output-stem
For local runs, each chunk is written to <output_dir>/<stem>/<stem>-chunk-<index>.root, with indices starting at zero. Grid submission includes the stem in each output filename suffix. The deprecated spelling output remains accepted as a compatibility alias.
Default value: the sample name
n-chunks
Number of output chunks for the sample. The value must be a positive integer. --n-chunks overrides this setting. Grid submission can also override it with --files-per-job. The deprecated spelling chunks remains accepted.
Default value: 1
stride
Specifies how to stride through the events of the sample; it must be a positive integer.
Default value: None (no striding)
n-events
Limits the maximum number of events to process for the sample; it must be a non-negative integer. The command-line --n-events option overrides this setting. Limits are ignored with a warning for multiple chunks. Grid submission rejects event limits because they do not compose reliably with file-based jobs. The deprecated spelling n-events-max remains accepted.
Default value: None (no limit)
campaign (optional)
Specifies the campaign used to discover sample input files when neither a per-sample input source nor a global input_dir is provided. Not supported for grid submission. prod_tag is deprecated; use campaign instead.
output_dir (optional)
Specifies the directory for local output files. Required for script-defined samples and for direct input without a single explicit output file; it can also be supplied with --output-dir. Test mode does not require it.
output_format (optional)
Specifies the output ROOT file format. Accepted values are ttree and rntuple.
Default: follow the format of the events TTree or RNTuple in the first input file. An explicit command-line option overrides this setting.
input_dir (optional)
Global directory containing sample subdirectories. For grid XRootD submission this must be an EOS path or XRootD directory URL; it overrides campaign discovery and is overridden by a per-sample input source.
input_lfn_list (optional)
Path to a .txt file containing DIRAC LFNs for grid submission. It defines one independent input sample and cannot be combined with script-defined samples or input_dir. Command-line input overrides this setting; without an override, the local runner rejects LFN configurations except in test mode, which uses a separate test file.
analysis_name (optional)
Optional name for the analysis
Default value: empty string
n_threads (optional)
Number of threads the RDataFrame will use during processing. To use all threads available on the machine specify -1.
Default value: 1
include_paths (optional)
Specify additional local header files to be JIT compiled. During grid submission, relative paths are resolved below the analysis-script directory and shipped to every worker through the input sandbox.
Default value: None
batch_queue (optional)
Batch queue name when running on HTCondor.
Default value: "longlunch"
comp_group (optional)
Computing account when running on HTCondor.
Default value: "group_u_FCC.local_gen"
output_dir_eos (optional)
Output directory on EOS, recognized only when submitting to HTCondor. If specified files will be copied there once the batch job is done. A string (str) or a template (string.Template) can be provided. In case of the template only one variable is currently supported: $timestamp.
Default value: None
eos_type (optional)
Type of the EOS proxy to be used.
Default value: user
test_file (optional)
Location of the file used with --test. Accepts a string or a string.Template with $key4hep_os, $key4hep_stack, and $date. The --test-file option overrides this setting. If neither is set, test mode reports an error.
graph (optional)
The computational graph of the analysis will be generated.
Default value: False
graph_path (optional)
Location where the computational graph of the analysis should be stored. Only paths with .dot and .png extensions are accepted.
Default value: empty string
use_data_source (optional)
User can specify how to provide physical object collections to the analyzers. If True the events will be loaded through the EDM4hep RDataSource.
Default value: False
do_weighted (optional)
Whether to use weighted or raw events. If True the events will be weighted with EDM4hep's EventHeader.weight and all normalisation factors calculated with sum of weights accordingly.
Default value: False
n_events (optional)
Maximum number of events per sample. A per-sample n-events or the command-line --n-events option takes precedence. Grid submission rejects this setting. The deprecated spelling n_events_max remains accepted.
